title: Offline bundle signing – Release Engineering implementation plan (draft)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working implementation plan for adding a signing stage to the release pipeline for Redwood Private “offline bundles” (air-gapped install path).
- Audience: Release Eng + Build/CI + Security review.
- This is not the bundle format spec; it’s the “how we’ll ship it” plan.

Owner / DRI
- DRI: Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering)
- Build/CI: Sahana Iyer
- Release tooling changes (bundle assembly + publish): Devon Price
- KMS/HSM + key ops: Hanae Suzuki (w/ Neha Kapoor for infra approvals)
- Security review: Marcus Lin
- Installer verify integration (consumer): Ethan Park (separate plan, but pipeline must match installer assumptions)

Problem statement
Air-gapped customers need to move Redwood Private artifacts via removable media/offline repos. We need cryptographic integrity + provenance guarantees that do not depend on any online verification. This requires:
- Deterministic manifest/digests for everything inside the bundle
- A bundle-level signature that can be verified offline (fail-closed)
- A clear publication layout so customers can keep bundle + detached signatures together

Non-goals (v1)
- Customer-managed signing (customer provides keys and signs Redwood artifacts)
- Replacing existing online distribution flows (this is offline bundle path only)

Definition of done (Release Eng scope)
1) CI produces an offline bundle artifact for Private releases (staging + prod) with:
   - Bundle payload (OCI images export + charts + binaries)
   - Bundle manifest w/ deterministic ordering and per-artifact digests
   - Provenance pointers (commit SHAs, build IDs; SBOM reference or embedded SBOM per spec)
2) CI signs the bundle manifest (or signing envelope) using KMS/HSM-backed key.
3) CI publishes:
   - bundle tarball
   - detached signature
   - public verification material (e.g., cert chain / public key) and versioned “trusted roots” for installer
4) CI fails hard on signing issues (no unsigned bundles published in prod).
5) Re-run/retry behavior is well-defined and does not produce ambiguous outputs.

High-level architecture (pipeline)
- Build artifacts (existing): container images + binaries + charts
- Assemble offline bundle (new/expanded): create a deterministic bundle directory + bundle manifest
- Generate provenance metadata (build ID, workflow run ID, commit SHAs, repo refs)
- Sign (new): create signing envelope / detached signature over canonicalized manifest
- Publish (new): upload bundle + signature + manifest + provenance pointers to artifact storage
- Promote to prod (existing gates + new verification that signature exists + matches manifest)

Signing approach (implementation assumption; confirm with Security)
- Bundle-level signing + per-artifact digests in manifest.
- Sign canonical bytes of bundle manifest (or spec-defined signing envelope that includes the manifest digest).
- Detached signature stored alongside bundle (e.g., .sig) + signer public key distributed with installer.
- Key stored in KMS/HSM; signing happens in CI via short-lived auth (OIDC -> KMS) and audit logs.

Workstreams and task breakdown

A) Release tooling changes (Devon) – bundle assembly + manifest determinism
- [ ] Confirm canonical manifest generation rules (ordering, JSON canonicalization, newline handling). This is the #1 cause of “works locally, fails in installer”.
- [ ] Update bundle builder to output:
  - bundle.tar.zst (or tar.gz; TBD by perf/compat)
  - manifest.json (human-readable but canonicalizable)
  - manifest.lock (optional: exact canonical bytes hash used for signing)
  - provenance.json (build metadata)
  - sbom/ (optional dir) or sbom references
- [ ] Ensure all file paths inside the tar are stable (no timestamps, no uid/gid drift, stable permissions).
- [ ] Images: choose export format used by installer (oci-layout vs docker-archive). Ensure the digest in manifest corresponds to the exported bytes we ship.
- [ ] Helm charts: ensure chart packaging is deterministic (Chart.yaml normalization; stable tgz output). (ref: redwood-helm-charts work)
- [ ] Binaries: include sha256 and size; ensure we hash the shipped bytes.
- [ ] “Release metadata” fields: release version, build id, commit SHAs for each repo (redwood, redwood-private-installer, redwood-helm-charts).
- [ ] Unit tests:
  - same inputs => identical manifest bytes
  - manifest digests match artifacts in the bundle

B) CI/CD pipeline changes (Sahana) – add signing stage + publishing
Target repos:
- redwood (main release pipeline; produces artifacts)
- potentially separate workflow for “offline bundle packaging” if we want to decouple from main release cadence

Tasks
- [ ] Add pipeline stage: “assemble-offline-bundle”
  Inputs: list of OCI images (digests), chart packages, binaries from build stages.
  Outputs: bundle + manifest + provenance.
- [ ] Add pipeline stage: “sign-offline-bundle”
  Inputs: canonical manifest bytes (or manifest digest) + metadata required by signing envelope.
  Outputs: signature file + signer identity metadata.
- [ ] Add pipeline stage: “publish-offline-bundle”
  Upload bundle tarball + manifest + signature + provenance to artifact store.
- [ ] Add pre-publish assertion: signature exists + verifies against the manifest generated in the same run.
- [ ] Add promotion gate: prod publish requires signature verification pass; no manual override in CI (break-glass belongs in installer + explicit audit).

Implementation details (CI)
- Auth to KMS/HSM:
  - use CI OIDC identity to assume signer role (no long-lived credentials)
  - enforce conditions: repo, workflow name, branch/tag pattern, environment
- Key usage constraints:
  - only allow signing for “release tags” (e.g., redwood-private-vX.Y.Z) and/or release branches
  - block PR workflows from hitting prod signing key
- Artifact storage layout (proposal; align with Infra):
  /private/offline-bundles/<version>/
    - redwood-private-offline-bundle-<version>.tar.zst
    - redwood-private-offline-bundle-<version>.manifest.json
    - redwood-private-offline-bundle-<version>.sig
    - redwood-private-offline-bundle-<version>.provenance.json
    - redwood-private-offline-bundle-<version>.sbom.json (if embedded)
    - SIGNING-KEYS/<key-id>/public.pem (or equivalent)
- Retention:
  - keep at least N minor versions + last N patch versions; regulated customers may ask for longer retention.

C) Key management / environments (Hanae + Marcus) – required before prod signing
Environments
- dev: test key, ephemeral; used for integration tests and PR validation
- staging: staging signing key (KMS), used for pre-prod release candidates
- prod: production signing key (KMS/HSM), used for GA releases only

Tasks
- [ ] Create KMS keys (staging + prod) with:
  - non-exportable private key
  - explicit key policy tied to CI workload identity
  - CloudTrail/audit logging enabled
- [ ] Define signer identity + provenance logging fields we must capture (for compliance evidence):
  - workflow run ID, commit SHA, tag, build timestamp, artifact digests
- [ ] Document access controls and “break glass” procedure for key compromise (owned by SecOps, but Release Eng needs operational hooks).
- [ ] Define rotation approach:
  - we must keep old public keys available for verification of previously shipped bundles
  - rotation cadence target (e.g., annual or after incident)

D) Integration tests / hermetic verification (Sahana + Ethan)
- [ ] Add pipeline job that:
  - assembles a small test bundle
  - signs with dev key
  - runs installer verification in “no network” mode (container net=none) and confirms PASS
  - flips one byte in payload and expects FAIL
- [ ] Add determinism test: build twice from same inputs => signature verifies for each bundle; manifests identical (or if artifacts differ, manifests must differ deterministically).

E) Release process / rollout plan (Connor)
- [ ] Dry run in staging:
  - produce signed bundles for 2 consecutive RCs
  - verify installer consumption in lab (air-gapped simulation)
- [ ] Canary in prod:
  - first GA release: publish signed bundle as “preview” alongside existing artifacts (if any), but do not route customers until SE sign-off
  - second GA release: mark as recommended path for air-gapped deployments
- [ ] Support readiness:
  - include “how to fetch bundle + signature” steps in internal release checklist
  - establish escalation path for verification failures (Release Eng vs Installer vs Sec)

Milestones (rough / align with project phases)
Phase 0 (requirements + threat model) – week 1–2
- Output: finalized signing approach assumptions + key custody decisions
- Dependencies: Security review sign-off on bundle-level signing scheme and key management direction

Phase 1 (bundle format + signing in staging) – week 3–6
- M1: deterministic manifest generation merged (tooling)
- M2: signing stage in staging pipeline working end-to-end
- M3: artifacts published to staging bucket w/ stable paths

Phase 2 (installer verification + end-to-end lab) – week 7–10
- M4: installer verifies staging-produced bundles offline
- M5: integration test job runs in CI and gates merges

Phase 3 (pilot customers) – week 11–13
- M6: first pilot bundle signed with prod key and verified by SE in customer-like environment
- M7: triage playbook for verification failures

Phase 4 (GA readiness) – week 14+
- M8: key rotation plan + monitoring in place

Risks / gotchas (notes from prior incidents)
- Manifest canonicalization: If the signature covers non-canonical JSON, verification will be flaky across implementations. Decide once and lock it.
- “Digest of what?” problems:
  - OCI image digest in registry != digest of exported archive bytes. Installer must verify the same thing we sign.
- Chart packaging drift:
  - Helm chart tgz output can vary if timestamps/ordering differ. Enforce deterministic packaging.
- CI retries producing different outputs:
  - need clear strategy: either disallow retries for signing step, or ensure retry reuses same manifest bytes.
- Key permission creep:
  - do not allow broad KMS Sign permissions. Tight workload identity constraints.
- Time-based fields:
  - keep timestamps out of canonical-signed content (or isolate them into unsigned provenance object).

Open questions (need answers before we finalize)
1) Exactly what bytes do we sign?
   - Option A: canonical JSON bytes of manifest.json
   - Option B: hash of manifest + additional envelope fields; sign the envelope
   Action: Marcus + Connor to align with ADR.

2) What verification material ships with installer?
   - Single public key pinned (simpler)
   - Keyring (supports rotation)
   Action: Hanae + Ethan.

3) Where do we store bundles + signatures for air-gapped customers?
   - S3/GCS w/ customer download; also allow “export to customer-provided offline repo” (Artifactory/Nexus)
   Action: Irene (Infra constraints) + Connor.

4) SBOM/provenance embedding vs linking
   - Some air-gapped envs prefer fully self-contained bundle
   Action: Devon + Naomi (Compliance) input.

Concrete next steps (Jan)
- Connor: schedule 30-min decision meeting on “bytes-to-sign” + canonicalization (w/ Marcus, Ethan, Devon, Sahana)
- Sahana: draft CI workflow changes in redwood repo behind feature flag OFFLINE_BUNDLE_SIGNING=on
- Devon: implement deterministic manifest generator + tests (start with charts + binaries; then images export)
- Hanae: open internal ticket for staging KMS key + policy; propose prod policy template

Appendix: proposed checklist for release manager (future)
- [ ] Confirm offline bundle build succeeded
- [ ] Confirm signature verification job passed
- [ ] Confirm artifacts present at /private/offline-bundles/<version>/
- [ ] Confirm public keys bundle updated (if rotated)
- [ ] Notify SE team of new signed bundle for pilots
